drugRefs.why: Provides reliable coverage of gram-negative enteric organisms and anaerobes, the dominant pathogens in cholangitis, and is appropriate first-line per Tokyo Guidelines for moderate-severe disease.

drugRefs.dose: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h + Metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h
drugRefs.coverage: Equally effective combination covering gram-negatives and anaerobes; useful when piperacillin-tazobactam is unavailable or contraindicated.

drugRefs.regimenLabel: Meropenem (if prior biliary instrumentation, MDR risk, or severe/grade III disease)
drugRefs.coverage: Broader option for patients with prior resistant organism isolation or severe disease per Tokyo Guidelines grading.

coverageMatrix.completeness: Piperacillin-tazobactam alone covers enterococcus in addition to gram-negatives and anaerobes, making it a more complete single-agent choice.
gaps: Vancomycin-resistant enterococcus is not covered by either regimen — relevant only with prior VRE colonization history.

stewardship.deescalation: Once biliary drainage is achieved and blood/bile cultures identify a susceptible organism, narrow to the most targeted single agent and limit total duration to 4-7 days from the time of adequate source control.

framework: Antibiotics alone do not resolve cholangitis if biliary obstruction persists — urgent source control (ERCP, percutaneous drainage, or surgery) is essential and should not be delayed while awaiting antibiotic response.
Limit duration to 4-7 days once adequate source control (drainage) has been achieved — antibiotics are frequently continued longer than necessary in this setting.
De-escalate based on bile/blood culture results once drainage is achieved and the patient is improving.
